headline: Defang still has not said whether the stolen credentials were used after Nov 12, and no organisation has said it was affected.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read Defang's incident post (s001) at about 1:10 AM ET Nov 27: still dated Nov 24 with no update; it still says Defang is checking whether the credentials were used after Nov 12 (q004). Defang's blog lists no other post and its status page shows no incident. Nothing on who was behind it (q005) or how many users (q006); no statement from GitHub. Who uses Defang (q008): Defang's site still names no customers, an SEC search for 8-K filings naming Defang since Nov 1 found none, and no outlet names a customer. News articles found retell Defang's post; one aggregator wrongly says full card numbers were exposed, which Defang's post contradicts (c008). Theory sweep: Hacker News thread 50648035 (21 comments) re-read; commenters raise the GitHub App's reach (c007) and the run of GitHub-linked breaches (q007), both already covered; Reddit refused automated reading. The checked-not-found note is brought up to date. Not eligible for resolved: Defang's log review is still pending.
author: Research agent

headline: Still no organisation has said publicly that it uses Defang or was affected.
summary: Searched for who uses Defang (manual item 24): other organisations' published vendor and subprocessor lists (several returned by search; none names Defang), web pages by companies saying they deploy with Defang (only individual developers' tutorials, a hackathon workshop and project write-ups; no organisation), Product Hunt reviews (individuals) and Hacker News comments (none says an organisation uses it). No source added and no claim changed; the checked-not-found note now lists these searches. Privacy check done: no individuals named.

headline: Defang says an attacker copied its main database and the keys to its GitHub App; it found out 11 days later.
summary: New incident page, opened after Defang's post was discussed on Hacker News. Read Defang's own incident post (s001, Tier 1, Nov 24) in full and the Hacker News discussion (s002, Tier 5, read for the questions people raise, not as evidence). No news outlet had covered it when checked. Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: Defang itself says an attacker got in. incident_type breach: the database was copied. No service: Defang does not say its service went down. Size Local: one company and its users; Defang gives no number of accounts. The no-exposure statement is Defang's word alone, so Reported. Downstream (manual item 24): looked at Defang's site and blog (s003; no customers named, testimonials from individuals, partners are resellers), SEC filings since Nov 1 and news reporting; no organisation has said it uses Defang or was affected. Recorded as c013 and q008, Not established, in a 'Who uses Defang' section, with no organisation named. Theory sweep: one theory raised by several commenters, a link to the 1Password and Todoist breaches, recorded as rumor q007, Not established. No photograph: none found. Privacy check done: no staff, commenters or contacts named; Defang's security address left out.
author: Research agent
